Exact unit cumulants of the skew-normal log-likelihood derivatives

sn_cumulants.Rd

Computes, by adaptive quadrature, the expected values of products of derivatives of the skew-normal log-density with respect to the reduced parameter \((\eta, \sigma, \alpha)\), where \(\eta\) is the location. These are the building blocks of the Fisher information, of the Cox and Snell second-order bias and of the bias-reducing adjusted scores.

Usage

sn_cumulants(alpha, sigma = 1, rel.tol = 1e-11)

Arguments

alpha

shape parameter (scalar).

sigma

scale parameter (scalar, default 1).

rel.tol

relative tolerance passed to [stats::integrate()].

Value

A list with components `k2` (3 x 3), `k3`, `k21` and `k111` (3 x 3 x 3 arrays), indexed by `c("eta", "sigma", "alpha")`. For `k21` the first two indices refer to the second derivative and the third to the first derivative.

Examples

cu <- sn_cumulants(3)
-cu$k2   # unit Fisher information at sigma = 1
#>             eta       sigma       alpha
#> eta   3.0281308  1.03041365  0.16115529
#> sigma 1.0304137  2.24420447 -0.08140149
#> alpha 0.1611553 -0.08140149  0.02713383
